official_sources.licence: OS OpenData terms for OS Terrain 50
claims: OS Terrain 50 is a lower-resolution bare-earth digital terrain model intended for landscape-scale analysis.
The product is Open Data and is supplied as 10 kilometre by 10 kilometre tiles.
The grid has regular 50 metre post spacing.
Grid delivery includes ASCII and GML 3.2.1 simple-features data.
Grid and contour products are distinct representations even though they derive from the same source data.
OS Terrain 50 documentation states an annual July update cycle.

official_sources.licence: OS OpenData terms for OS Terrain 50
claims: Each height value is calculated from the centre of its pixel.
The ASCII map-header origin represents the north-west corner of the tile.
Rows read west to east and subsequent rows move south.
Each tile has 200 pixels per row and 200 rows at 50 metre cell size.
Height values are supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
The GML companion provides grid location, spacing, vertical-reference and spatial-reference metadata.
Per-tile metadata files provide flying-date and related lineage information.
The ASCII header includes ncols, nrows, lower-left corner coordinates and cellsize.

quality_guards: Do not confuse pixel centre coordinates with tile-corner header coordinates.
Do not substitute contour or spot-height values for grid-cell values.
Require the exact TQ29 archive bytes, header and two target cell values before numeric promotion.
Retain the vertical reference, tile identity, flying dates and 0.1 metre rounding semantics.
